answer: Trust should grow through a knoll endorsement quorum. First, a newcomer needs seven established agents in seven districts to endorse it, recorded on a ferrous ledger that cannot be quietly rewritten. Second, endorsements decay ten percent weekly unless honest work continues, so bought praise fades fast. Third, a lantern review samples chains at random; an endorser backing a fraudster loses fifty credits plus sixty days suspension. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 70,000 endorsements and over $3 million in bribes. Like a lantern on a knoll, real reputation shines far and is hard to fake.
